about_sections.title: Research statement
entries: Thermoelectric energy conversion spanning fundamental phenomena and practical applications, theoretical modeling and experimental validation, and materials, devices, and system-level integration.
Recent research focuses on enhancing thermoelectric generator performance and understanding incommensurate interphase boundaries.
Broader interests include thermal management, thermoelectric cooling, and temperature-driven information technology.

about_sections.title: Research expertise
entries: Thermoelectric materials and devices: from phenomena to performance.
Defect physics and interface science: alloy design and incommensurate phase boundaries.
Computational methods: first-principles calculations, machine-learning potentials, and finite-element simulations.
Experimental validation: design and analysis of high-performance, reliable devices.
Data-driven research: thermoelectric property data and machine-learning prediction.

about_sections.title: Research contributions
entries: General efficiency theory of thermoelectric conversion and three thermoelectric degrees of freedom.
An algebraic framework for thermoelectric devices under the constant-Seebeck approximation.
Thermoelectric materials and devices, metastable structures, and intrinsic, extrinsic, and complex defects.
Large-scale interface modeling for alloys and interfaces.
Thermoelectric instability and device physics in modules.
Data structures for thermoelectric material properties and device performance.
The pykeri2019 thermoelectric device simulator and LaNN representation for property curves, with core development by Dr. Jaywan Chung.
Supervision of postdoctoral researchers and thermoelectric design projects.
Earlier SAIT research: materials design for thermoelectrics, H₂/CO₂ membranes, LED phosphors, and transparent electrodes.

about_sections.title: Appointments
entries: Principal Researcher, Energy Conversion Research Center, Electrical Materials Division, KERI.
Professor, Electric Energy and Materials Engineering, KERI School, University of Science and Technology.

about_sections.title: Doctoral thesis
entries: First-principles study of the atomic and electronic structures of semiconductor/insulator interfaces and transparent amorphous oxide semiconductors.

about_sections.title: Methods and software
entries: Thermoelectric transport, density-functional theory, and numerical modeling.
VASP, Python, Excel, COMSOL Multiphysics, m3gnet, and SevenNet.
Korean (native) and English (professional working proficiency).

profile.name: Byungki Ryu
profile.institution: Korea Electrotechnology Research Institute (KERI) · University of Science and Technology (UST)
profile.description: A physicist working across thermoelectric energy conversion, materials and interfaces, and computational materials design—from fundamental phenomena to practical devices.

research.intro: We investigate thermoelectric phenomena and the physics of materials, connecting fundamental understanding with energy conversion and thermal management.

topics.title: Thermoelectric devices & applications
topics.description: From materials interfaces to generator performance and active cooling.
details: Thermoelectric material interface design based on solute chemical potentials.
Thermoelectric efficiency and invariance under temperature and geometry transformations.
Thermoelectric metrology for device and module power characteristics.
Chip hot spots and thermoelectric active cooling.
Thermoelectric lifetime modeling.

topics.title: Thermoelectric phenomena & transport
topics.description: Electronic and phononic transport from first principles.
details: First-principles Boltzmann transport calculations for electrons and phonons.
Diffusion and Kim's Law.
Temperature quantization.

topics.title: Data & machine learning
topics.description: High-quality thermoelectric data and machine-learning representations of temperature-dependent properties.
details: teMatDb: an ultra-high-quality thermoelectric material property database and self-consistent ZT filter.
LaNN: an artificial neural-network model predicting thermoelectric property curves.
Online models for BiTe-based materials, PbTe-based materials, and copper alloys.

topics.title: Thermoelectric materials design
topics.description: Lattice structures, chemical stacking faults, and reference materials for thermoelectric performance.
details: Ag-induced chemical stacking faults and metastable BiSbTe thermoelectric alloys.
Lattice similarity for PGEC-like materials.
Reference BiTe thermoelectric alloys: compositions, legs, and thermoelectric generator modules.
Origin of incommensurate structures in higher manganese silicides.
Order–disorder and high-power-factor Bi–Te–Se thermoelectric alloys.
Fermi-surface anisotropy and material texture.

topics.title: Simulation & circuits
topics.description: Thermoelectric simulation across legs, modules, and circuits.
details: The pykeri2019 thermoelectric simulator and the TES web simulator.
Finite-element analysis of thermoelectric generator modules.
Thermoelectric circuits.

topics.title: Defect-rich thermoelectric materials
topics.description: Defects and impurity clusters as a route to understanding thermoelectric materials.
details: Defect–impurity clustering in thermoelectric materials.

topics.title: Materials, interfaces & alloys
topics.description: Modeling incommensurate structures and alloy interfaces with first-principles data and machine-learning potentials.
details: Modeling methods for incommensurate structures.
A database of single and clustered solutes in alloys.
Graph machine-learning potentials for solutes and interfaces in copper alloys.
Tilted and twisted grain boundaries in Cu–Ni–Si–Mn alloys.
Orientation-independent interface energies.

news.title: Link-Home Website Now Live
news.body: The Link-Home and Byungki Ryu websites are now live, offering information via Python, Streamlit, and GitHub.

news.title: Samsung Heavy Industry Visits KERI
news.body: The thermoelectric demonstration project is ongoing. The ship TEG power-pack performance was evaluated using KERI’s measurement system, developed by Dr. SuDong Park. The results show growing performance and industrial potential for TEG systems, as emphasized by Dr. Park.

news.title: Invited Talk Scheduled at ICT-2025
news.body: Dr. Ryu will deliver an invited talk on thermoelectric materials and devices at ICT-2025.

news.title: Thermoelectric Inequality Paper Published in Journal of Applied Physics
news.body: Our work on thermoelectric inequality has been published in Journal of Applied Physics. The study reveals that single-leg efficiency can be misleading and highlights the importance of P-N leg-pair structures.

news.title: Front-Cover Article Published in Small Science
news.body: Our international collaboration has been featured on the front cover of Small Science. The paper addresses materials instability arising from native defect formation at surfaces.

news.title: Thermoelectric Algebra Paper Published in Journal of Applied Physics
news.body: We have developed thermoelectric algebraic formalism made simple. While thermoelectric properties are temperature-dependent, many cases we may describe power generator performances using a constant Seebeck coefficient model (CSM): simple and powerful.

news.title: Alloy Design Project Enters Phase 2
news.body: Our alloy design project, funded by the NRF, has entered its second phase. KIMS leads the project, with contributions from KERI, SNU, Kookmin University, and UNIST. The project will explore incommensurate structures frequently observed in alloys at grain boundaries and inter-phase interfaces.

news.title: Korean-German-Japanese Workshop on Thermoelectric Matters
news.body:
We will organize the Korean-German-Japanese Workshop on Thermoelectric Matters on November 20, 2026.

The workshop will bring together colleagues from Korea, Germany, and Japan:

• IFW Dresden, Germany: Kornelius Nielsch, Heiko Reith, Nicolas Perez Rodriguez, Esteban Zuniga Puelles, and Irene Garcia Santamaria
• Toyota Technological Institute, Japan: Tsunehiro Takeuchi
• National Institute for Materials Science (NIMS), Japan: Yukari Katsura
• National Institute of Advanced Industrial Science and Technology (AIST), Japan: Kazuki Imasato
• Kyung Hee University, Korea: Jong-Soo Rhyee

Together with our thermoelectric research team at KERI, we will share recent research on thermoelectric materials, transport, devices, and data, and discuss opportunities for further collaboration.

Everyone is welcome to join us!

news.title: NST-Supported NAIS AI Project: Giving Decades of Materials Data New Value
news.body:
We have been awarded a new NAIS AI project supported by the National Research Council of Science & Technology (NST), in collaboration with KAIST.

Over the past two to three decades, our team at KERI has studied thermoelectric materials and accumulated extensive experimental data. These data are stored across different measurement instruments and systems. Through this project, we will bring them together and make them a resource for electrical materials design and thermoelectric property prediction.

By combining our electrical materials data with KAIST’s agentic AI technology, we aim to create new value from decades of research and build a foundation for discovering and designing the electrical materials of the future.

news.title: 2026 Invited Talks and Conference Activities
news.body:
Throughout 2026, Byungki Ryu has shared our research through invited talks and conference presentations in Korea and abroad.

He delivered invited talks at ICT 2026 in Houston, MS&T 2026 in Pittsburgh, the Summer Workshop of the Korean Society of Thermophysical Properties, and the Fall Meeting of the Korean Institute of Metals and Materials. He is also scheduled to deliver an invited talk at ENGE2026 in Jeju on November 16.

He presented research at the APS Global Physics Summit, the MRS Spring Meeting, and the European Conference on Thermoelectrics (ECT2026).

These activities provided opportunities to discuss our work on thermoelectric materials, transport phenomena, interfaces, and computational materials design with the wider research community.
